/.title: PlayTurf – Online Cricket & Sports Turf Booking Platform
/.description: PlayTurf is an online sports turf booking platform: discover cricket, football, futsal and box-cricket turfs near you, check live slot availability, and book courts by the hour — plus open games to join and split costs.
/.h1: PlayTurf – Discover and Book Sports Turfs Online

sections.body: PlayTurf lists sports venues with their location, facilities, operating hours and hourly rates. Browse turfs by city, filter by sport, and open a venue page for photos, amenities and genuine player reviews. Discovery pages are built from the platform's live venue database — cities and sports appear only when venues actually exist.

Venues on PlayTurf commonly offer football, cricket, futsal and box-cricket courts. Pick your sport, compare venues and hourly prices, and reserve a specific court for a specific hour. Multi-hour bookings reserve consecutive slots in one go, so nobody can take the hour in between.

Choose a date, pick a free start slot, select a court, set your duration (1 to 12 hours) and confirm. You receive a booking ID and a downloadable ticket to show at the venue. Bookings can be cancelled within a short window right after confirmation.

sections.h2: Check Turf Availability and Time Slots
sections.body: Every venue shows real-time slot availability for the selected date. Booked slots are marked unavailable, venues with several courts show availability per court, and reservations pending payment expire automatically so stale holds never block a free slot.

Player accounts keep your booking history: upcoming and past sessions, cancellations, and downloadable tickets. Open Games let you join games hosted by other players and pay your share of the court instead of the full slot price.

Live availability instead of phone calls, transparent hourly pricing set by venues, instant confirmation with a booking ID, and open games for solo players. PlayTurf distinguishes platform-operated venues from independent partner venues — partner facilities are never presented as PlayTurf-owned.

body: What is PlayTurf? An online sports turf discovery and booking platform for five-a-side football, cricket, futsal and more.
How can I book a cricket turf? Open a cricket venue, pick a date and a free slot, choose the court and confirm — you get an instant booking ID.
Can I book multiple hours? Yes — up to 12 consecutive hours in a single booking.
How do I check turf availability? Each venue page shows live slot availability for the date you pick.
How can I manage my booking? Open it from My Bookings to view, download the ticket or cancel within the allowed window.
How can I contact PlayTurf? Use the in-app feedback channel — see /contact for details.

/about.title: About PlayTurf | PlayTurf
/about.description: PlayTurf is an online sports turf discovery and booking platform: find football grounds, cricket pitches, futsal and box-cricket courts, check live slot availability and book by the hour.

sections.body: PlayTurf is an online sports turf discovery and booking platform. Players browse listed venues — football grounds, cricket pitches, futsal courts and box-cricket cages — see each venue's hourly rates, facilities and operating hours, and book a specific court for a specific hour directly from the site. Venue owners list their facilities so local players can find and book them without phone calls or manual coordination.

Booking a turf slot traditionally means calling venues, waiting for confirmation and hoping nobody else took the hour. PlayTurf replaces that with live availability: every venue shows which slots are free for a chosen date, and a confirmed booking reserves that exact court and hour. Multi-hour bookings reserve consecutive slots in one transaction, and Open Games let individual players join hosted games and split the court cost instead of paying for a full slot alone.

Two groups: players, who discover venues, book slots and join open games; and venue owners (turf partners), who list their facilities, manage their courts and see their bookings through the venue-owner dashboard. The platform serves casual five-a-side groups, box-cricket squads and individual players looking for a game.

Venues are browsable by city and by sport. Each venue page shows photos, the sports offered, facilities such as floodlights and parking, operating hours, the hourly rate and genuine player reviews. City and sport pages (for example turfs in Bangalore, or football turfs in Mumbai) only list venues that actually exist in the platform's live database.

Pick a venue, choose a date, pick a free start slot, choose the court where the venue has several, set the duration (one to twelve hours) and confirm. Consecutive slots are reserved together so nobody can take the hour in between. Bookings can be cancelled within a short window after confirmation, and every booking gets a downloadable ticket with a unique booking ID.

Payments on the platform currently run through a simulated checkout — bookings are confirmed without money moving while a live payment gateway is being integrated. Supported sports depend on the venues listed; common ones include football, cricket, futsal and basketball. PlayTurf does not claim venue ownership of partner facilities: each venue's ownership is shown as either PlayTurf-operated or an independent partner.

/contact.title: Contact PlayTurf | PlayTurf
/contact.description: How to reach PlayTurf: in-app support and feedback for players, venue-owner inquiries, and platform contact channels.

sections.body: The fastest way to reach PlayTurf support is inside the app: use the Provide Feedback option (found under More → Support and in venue-owner settings) to report a bug, a booking problem or a question. Messages go straight to the support team with your device context attached, and you can attach a screenshot.

For booking disputes or questions about a specific booking, open the booking from My Bookings — the booking detail page shows the venue, slot, payment record and ticket. Cancellations inside the allowed window can be done directly from the booking page. Anything else, send it through the feedback form and mention the booking ID.

Turf owners and facility managers can request a listing through the venue-owner (client) sign-in; the owner dashboard manages courts, slots and bookings for their venue. For listing inquiries or partnership questions, use the same feedback channel and select the appropriate category.

A published support email address and telephone line are being finalised and will be listed here once verified — PlayTurf does not publish contact details it cannot verify. Until then, the in-app feedback channel is the official support route and every message reaches the team.

/privacy.title: Privacy Policy — PlayTurf | PlayTurf
/privacy.description: How PlayTurf handles your data: account registration, booking details, authentication, storage with Supabase, notifications, and your choices.

sections.body: An account on PlayTurf consists of an authentication record (email or phone number, managed by Supabase Auth) and a profile row with your display name, phone number and chosen avatar. Bookings you create store the venue, date, time slots, duration, court, a booking ID and a payment reference. Open game participation stores your player name, avatar and join record. Feedback you submit stores the message you write plus technical context (device type, browser, operating system, screen size and the page you were on) to help reproduce issues.

Sign-in is handled by Supabase Authentication. PlayTurf supports email/password, Google sign-in and phone OTP. Sessions are stored locally in your browser (localStorage) and refreshed automatically; signing out removes them. Administrators can additionally enroll a second authentication factor (authenticator app), which Supabase verifies before granting admin access.

The platform checkout is currently simulated: bookings are confirmed without payment details being collected and no money moves. When a live payment gateway is integrated, this policy will be updated to describe exactly which payment data the gateway processes — payment card data is expected to be handled by the payment provider, not by PlayTurf servers.

When configured, PlayTurf uses two third-party services. PostHog (hosted at app.posthog.com) records product analytics events and may record sessions to help improve usability — form inputs are masked during recording. Sentry captures error reports and, on some sessions, replays the technical state of the app when something breaks. Both services receive technical data such as your IP address, device and browser characteristics. Analytics and monitoring are switched off unless the operator has configured them for the deployment you are using.

PlayTurf data is stored in Supabase (PostgreSQL database, authentication and file storage). Static assets and the site itself are served through Vercel. These providers process data on behalf of PlayTurf as part of operating the service.

PlayTurf does not use advertising cookies. It uses browser localStorage for your session, your selected theme, notification records and booking reminders. A service worker caches static assets so the app works offline; that cache lives on your device only.

Your profile and bookings are protected by row-level security: database rules restrict each account to its own records, and administrative access is role-restricted with privileged actions recorded in an append-only audit log. Aggregate, non-identifying statistics (for example total booking counts) may be shown in platform dashboards. Feedback messages are visible to the support team.

You can sign out and clear locally stored data at any time via your browser. Under India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 you can expect to be able to request access, correction and erasure of your personal data and to withdraw consent for future processing. While self-service tooling is being built, send such requests (and any privacy grievances) through the in-app feedback channel and they will be actioned. Booking and feedback records are retained for operational history; the platform does not claim a specific backup-deletion period.

This policy describes the platform’s actual behaviour at the time of writing and will be updated as features change (in particular when live payments are introduced). It has not yet been reviewed by legal counsel and does not constitute legal advice; a formal legal review is required before it is treated as the platform’s final privacy policy. A named grievance officer will be published here once appointed.

/blog.title: Playing Guides — Turf Booking Tips | PlayTurf
/blog.description: Practical guides for booking and playing on sports turfs: how to book, what to bring, and when slots are cheapest.

sections.h2: How to Book a Football Turf: A Step-by-Step Guide
sections.body: Pick your date and start time, choose how many hours you need (most 5-a-side games fit one hour), check that the court is free for that slot, confirm the price before paying, and keep the booking ID for entry. On PlayTurf you can do all of this from a venue's page: choose the date, pick a free slot, select a court, and confirm.

sections.h2: What to Bring to a 5-a-Side Turf Match
sections.body: Bring turf shoes or flat-soled trainers (studs are often not allowed on artificial turf), a filled water bottle per player, a dark and a light shirt so teams split easily, and shin guards for football. Most turfs provide the ball and goal nets, and many rent equipment — check the venue's amenities before you pack your own.

sections.h2: Peak vs Off-Peak Turf Slots: When to Book and Save
sections.body: Evenings after 6 PM and weekends are the peak hours at most turfs — they fill first and cost the most. Morning and early-afternoon slots on weekdays are the cheapest and quietest. On PlayTurf the price you see for each slot is the venue's own rate; booking a longer morning session often costs less than a single peak-hour slot.

sections.body: Pick your date and start time, choose how many hours you need (most 5-a-side games fit one hour), check that the court is free for that slot, confirm the price before paying, and keep the booking ID for entry. On PlayTurf you can do all of this from a venue's page: choose the date, pick a free slot, select a court, and confirm.

sections.heading: 1. Decide the slot length before you search
body: Most 5-a-side football games fit comfortably into a one-hour slot once you account for warm-up. If you want time for two full games or a longer practice session, book two consecutive hours rather than hoping the next hour stays free — consecutive slots are booked together so nobody else can take the hour in between.

sections.heading: 2. Check what the venue actually offers
body: Before booking, look for:
Surface type and whether floodlights are included in evening slots
Whether the venue has multiple courts — larger venues let your group book court 2 even when court 1 is taken
Amenities that matter to your group: parking, washrooms, drinking water, equipment rental

sections.heading: 3. Book the exact slot and court
body: On PlayTurf, open the venue page, pick your date from the strip, and select a start time. Slots already booked by someone else are shown as unavailable. If the venue has several courts, you pick the specific court — availability is checked per court, per hour, so two groups can play side by side.

sections.heading: 4. Confirm and keep the booking ID
body: After payment you get a booking with a unique ID and a ticket you can download or share with your group. The ticket shows the venue, date, start and end time, and court — show it at the venue. If your plans change immediately, cancellations are allowed within a short window right after booking; after that the slot belongs to you, so book carefully.

sections.heading: 5. Splitting the cost with your squad
body: If you don't have a full squad, Open Games lets you join games other players have opened and split the court cost — the host opens a slot, players join, and each player pays their share instead of the full court fee.

/blog/what-to-bring-to-a-turf-game.title: What to Bring to a 5-a-Side Turf Match | PlayTurf
/blog/what-to-bring-to-a-turf-game.description: The practical packing list for a box-cricket or 5-a-side football turf game — footwear, hydration, and the small items that save the evening.
/blog/what-to-bring-to-a-turf-game.h1: What to Bring to a 5-a-Side Turf Match

sections.body: Bring turf shoes or flat-soled trainers (studs are often not allowed on artificial turf), a filled water bottle per player, a dark and a light shirt so teams split easily, and shin guards for football. Most turfs provide the ball and goal nets, and many rent equipment — check the venue's amenities before you pack your own.

sections.heading: Footwear comes first
body: Artificial turf is abrasive and harder on joints than grass. Flat-soled turf shoes give the best grip on rubber-crumb surfaces. Metal or long studs sink into the turf and strain knees — many venues ban them. If you're buying your first pair, mid-range turf shoes are fine to start.

sections.heading: Team kit in two colours
body: The fastest way to split a mixed group is dark shirts versus light shirts. Bibs help, but most casual games just ask players to plan ahead. One playing ball per court is usually enough — confirm with the venue whether they provide one or you should bring your own.

sections.heading: Hydration and the small stuff
body: One litre of water per player per hour of play — turf radiates heat, especially in afternoon slots
A small towel and a change of shirt for after the game
Shin guards for football; batting gloves if your box-cricket venue doesn't rent them
A basic first-aid strip: plasters and an elastic bandage cover most turf scrapes

sections.heading: Before you leave the venue
body: Turf slots run back-to-back. Finish your game on time, collect bottles and tape, and report anything damaged to the venue staff — the next group's slot starts the moment yours ends.

/blog/peak-vs-off-peak-turf-slots.h1: Peak vs Off-Peak Turf Slots: When to Book and Save

sections.body: Evenings after 6 PM and weekends are the peak hours at most turfs — they fill first and cost the most. Morning and early-afternoon slots on weekdays are the cheapest and quietest. On PlayTurf the price you see for each slot is the venue's own rate; booking a longer morning session often costs less than a single peak-hour slot.

sections.heading: Why prices vary by hour
body: Turf operators set their own hourly rates and typically charge more when demand is highest — weekday evenings when office groups play, and weekend mornings and nights. Floodlit night slots carry the venue's lighting cost. None of this is a surcharge added at checkout: the rate you see for the slot is the venue's rate for that hour.

sections.heading: The cheapest good slots
body: Weekday mornings (roughly 6–10 AM): cool weather, empty courts, lowest rates
Weekday early afternoons: quiet, though hot in summer — bring extra water
Late-night slots where the venue runs them: floodlit and often cheaper than prime evening
Prime time — weekday 6–11 PM and weekends — books out first. If your group can only play prime time, book several days ahead.

sections.heading: Getting better value without chasing discounts
body: Three habits reliably reduce cost per player: book consecutive hours in one booking (one court fee, longer game), fill the squad (the court fee is per slot, not per player — ten players halve the per-head cost versus five), and use Open Games to split a slot with players you don't know yet.
